observed_failure_at_parent: RuntimeWarning: divide by zero encountered in divide (hits_alg.py:300); hub/authority scores become inf/NaN because the dominant eigenvector returned by np.linalg.eigh for path_graph(3) has a zero maximum (eigvals [0., 2., 2.], eigenvector [-0.707, 0., -0.707]), so h /= h.max() divides by 0.0. pytest: 1 failed (test_hits_numpy_normalized_false_finite), 10 deselected.
verified: FAIL at parent observed (pytest + direct call) with the buggy code (raw ev[:, np.argmax(e)] without abs) confirmed present by inspection; PASS at fix observed with np.abs confirmed present by inspection; regression test also passes as part of the full test_hits.py file at HEAD.
issue_paraphrase: For certain small undirected graphs, the non-normalized variant of the HITS hub/authority computation can return scores that are not finite numbers (infinity or NaN) or that come out negative, where non-negative finite scores are expected. The values are scaled by dividing by the largest component of the dominant eigenvector, and for graphs where that eigenvector has a zero maximum the division produces the invalid numbers. The internal eigenvector implementation is affected; the regression test calls it directly.
fix_summary: Canonicalize the sign of the two dominant eigenvectors returned by np.linalg.eigh by applying np.abs() before the max-scaling step, so the vector maximum can never be 0 and the resulting scores are non-negative and finite. (Root cause: eigh returns a dominant eigenvector with a zero component for the doubly degenerate largest eigenvalue of path_graph(3).)
notes: The bug lives in the internal _hits_numpy helper, which is not reachable from public nx.hits (default power_iteration, or method='svd'); the golden test calls the helper directly, so the task instruction must point at the failing test. Test is deterministic in this environment (numpy 2.5.3 / LAPACK). Whole test_hits.py file runs in <1s. Optional scipy from default.txt not needed for this test.

issue_paraphrase: Generating a geometric soft configuration graph while supplying the degree sequence as a dictionary of node-to-degree values raises a TypeError instead of producing a graph, because the generator sums the dictionary's keys rather than its values when it computes the mean degree. The function is documented to accept either a sequence of degrees or a mapping, but the mapping form crashes (or silently uses the node IDs instead of the degrees) whenever the node IDs are not numbers that happen to sum to the right value.
fix_summary: One-line fix: use sum(kappas.values()) instead of sum(kappas) when computing the mean degree from a dict, so the degrees themselves are averaged.

Container: bench-base:python-3.12, repo at /work/networkx; pip install -e /work/networkx && pip install -r requirements/test.txt (pytest). Pure python (stdlib GML reader/writer).
Parent direction:
  git config --global --add safe.directory /work/networkx
  git reset --hard b1f956344071ba1adfad17d56d62a7a78dfd37e6 && git clean -fd
  git checkout 304b3ae481c2027f6b6ff493715cdeb7043cb90d -- networkx/readwrite/tests/test_gml.py
  # prove buggy code present: in generate_gml the tuple-label branch emits the repr string WITHOUT escape()
  python - <<'PY'
  import networkx as nx
  G = nx.Graph(); G.add_node(('x"] node [ id 99 label "pwn', 'y'))
  data = '\n'.join(nx.generate_gml(G))
  print('"' in data, '"pwn' in data)
  H = nx.parse_gml(data); print(len(H), list(H))
  PY
  # => False True / 2 ["('x", "pwn','y')"] -- the raw quote closes the string early and injects a fake node
  python -m pytest 'networkx/readwrite/tests/test_gml.py::TestGraph::test_tuple_label_quote_escape' -p no:cacheprovider
Fix direction:
  git reset --hard 304b3ae481c2027f6b6ff493715cdeb7043cb90d && git clean -fd
  # prove fix present: grep -n 'escape(label)' networkx/readwrite/gml.py => 760: yield f'{indent}{key} "{escape(label)}"'
  same script => True False / 1 ["('x\"] node [ id 99 label \"pwn','y')"]
  same pytest line => 1 passed
observed_failure_at_parent: Generated GML for a node whose tuple-typed label contains a double quote contains the raw, unescaped quote (no '"' entity) so the closing quote of the GML string terminates the label early; parsing the output back yields 2 nodes ('("x', "pwn','y')") instead of the 1 node that was written -- crafted label content can inject arbitrary nodes/attributes. pytest: 1 failed (test_tuple_label_quote_escape), 25 deselected.
verified: FAIL at parent observed (round-trip injection demo + pytest) with unescaped label output confirmed by inspection ('"' absent, raw '"pwn' present in output); PASS at fix observed with escape(label) confirmed present by inspection; test passes in full test_gml.py at HEAD.
issue_paraphrase: Writing a graph to the GML format can produce invalid, unsafe output when a node label is a tuple whose string representation contains a double-quote character: the quote is emitted without escaping, so it closes the GML string early and lets the rest of the label be interpreted as graph content (extra nodes and attributes can be injected). Reading such a file back round-trips to a different, larger graph than the one that was written. Tuple node labels should be escaped exactly like plain string labels.
fix_summary: In generate_gml, route tuple-valued labels through the same escape() call that other quoted strings get: build the repr-based label string, then yield f'{indent}{key} "{escape(label)}"' so embedded quotes become " entities.
notes: Self-contained, deterministic, subsecond. Slight subtlety: the tuple-label branch must still be escaped while list/tuple node/edge attribute values that are NOT the label keep their old path, so the author should let the regression test drive the change. Whole test_gml.py: 26 tests, ~1s at 1 CPU.

  same python one-liner => 0.0
  same pytest line => 1 passed; full file 26 passed
observed_failure_at_parent: Group betweenness centrality reports 0.125 for the group {0,1,2} on an 8-edge graph where no shortest path between non-group nodes has an interior group node, so the correct value is 0 (matches plain betweenness reasoning). pytest: 1 failed (test_group_betweenness_no_paths_through_group), 25 passed. The companion test test_group_betweenness_many_groups (singleton groups vs plain betweenness) passes at parent too and also passes at fix.
verified: FAIL at parent observed (direct call returning 0.125 + pytest) with buggy code (denominator uses plain all-pairs sigma instead of group-aware sigma_m) confirmed present by inspection; PASS at fix observed (returns 0.0, full file 26 passed) with the sigma_m-based denominator and zero-denominator guard confirmed present by inspection.
issue_paraphrase: Group betweenness centrality can return a nonzero score for a group of nodes even though no shortest path between any two nodes outside the group passes through the group's interior, where the mathematically correct score is zero. The spurious contribution also makes singleton-group scores disagree with ordinary (per-node) betweenness centrality in some cases, and the discrepancy appears on small connected undirected graphs, so it is easy to hit in practice.
fix_summary: Change the 'has no path through group' term (dvxy) so the denominator uses the group-aware path counts sigma_m[v][y] (and sigma_m[x][y]) instead of the all-pairs sigma, and add an explicit guard skipping the update when sigma_m[x][y], sigma_m[x][v] or sigma_m[v][y] is 0, so the crossing-rate is 0 when no path goes through the group.
notes: Deterministic, subsecond for the golden test (5-9 node graphs); whole test_group.py (26 tests) ~0.3s at 1 CPU. The algorithm is intricate, so a solver must reason from the definition/tests rather than from the code alone -- this is a good medium/harder task. The upstream commit bundles two regression tests; the many_groups one passes both sides, the no_paths_through_group one is the failing golden test.
